title: Bank of America Survey Shows Investors Are Split on AI Bubble Risks
source_used: The WealthAdvisor's full account of Bank of America's October fund manager survey (Barron's page returns HTTP 401)
key_facts: Bank of America's October fund manager survey, conducted 2 to 8 Oct 2026 among 161 participants managing $453 billion in assets.
A net 37% of managers are overweight technology, up from 30% in September and the highest since August 2020.
45% believe an AI bubble will emerge in 2027; 42% disagree.
Long positions in global semiconductor stocks are the most crowded trade; cash holdings are 3.9%, below the 4% level that triggers the bank's contrarian sell signal.
A disorderly rise in yields ranks as the biggest perceived threat to markets, ahead of an AI bubble; the 10-year Treasury yield is around 5.19%.
19% of allocators say they are already shifting from stocks to bonds; 37% say a 6% 10-year yield would prompt them to move.
Bank of America's broad sentiment indicator fell to 6.4 from 7.0.
quote_evidence: Bank of America's October survey found a net 37% of managers overweight technology, up from 30% in September, while 45% believe an AI bubble will emerge in 2027.
The survey, conducted Oct. 2 through Oct. 8 among 161 participants, identified long positions in global semiconductor stocks as the market's most crowded trade.
A disorderly rise in yields ranks as the biggest perceived threat to global markets, ahead of an AI bubble.
why_it_matters_hint: Fund managers keep buying technology shares while nearly half expect an AI bubble.
event_date: survey of 2 to 8 Oct 2026, published 13 Oct 2026
notes: Barron's page returned HTTP 401. The same Bank of America survey was read in The WealthAdvisor's full account (thewealthadvisor.com); MarketWatch, Moomoo, Seeking Alpha and Yahoo Finance also carried it (headlines only seen).
